source_policy: Titles, authors and dates checked against original papers, publisher records or the project author's repository. Dates below prefer final publication over first arXiv submission. Industrial code is identified separately from peer-reviewed work.

references.title: Understanding and Detecting Software Upgrade Failures in Distributed Systems
references.venue: ACM SIGOPS 28th Symposium on Operating Systems Principles (SOSP '21)
references.metadata_evidence: Author-hosted paper page 1 lists full title, all seven authors, 2021 SOSP venue and DOI; page14 gives the artifact URL.
references.relevance: Upgrade-state testing and serialization compatibility are established research topics; DUPTester is a tool in this paper, not the paper title.
references.difference_to_our_claim: Our proposed contribution is a small curated coding-agent repair resource with executable artifact obligations, not a new upgrade-testing technique.

references.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
references.venue: The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024)
references.metadata_evidence: ICLR proceedings PDF first page confirms authors/title/conference year; arXiv record distinguishes 2023 submission and ICLR2024 publication.
references.relevance: Repository-level issue repair and patch execution provide the general task precedent; existing benchmark issues can include historical compatibility.
references.difference_to_our_claim: Specialist producer/artifact contracts and a compact reusable task interface, not first real-repository repair or first historical-file task.

references.title: SWE-Gate: Passing Functional Tests Is Not Enough for Software Engineering Agents
references.metadata_evidence: Original arXiv record gives all six authors and 2026-09-03 submission; no peer-reviewed venue is claimed here.
references.relevance: Separate functional and review-constraint tests with released noncompliant/gold patches are already an explicit agent-evaluation design.
references.difference_to_our_claim: Real historical producer bytes and artifact continuation contracts are the specialist resource focus. Do not claim first non-functional acceptance layer, or compare only against its functional tests.

references.title: GitChameleon 2.0: Evaluating AI Code Generation Against Python Library Version Incompatibilities
references.venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
references.metadata_evidence: ACL Anthology citation/BibTeX confirms final year2026 and full author name Muawiz Sajjad Chaudhary. Project-page recommended misc entry still says2025; prefer the final ACL record.
references.relevance: Version-conditioned API code generation with executable visible/hidden tests is already benchmarked.
references.difference_to_our_claim: Repairing a reader to accept immutable objects written by another process/version differs from generating client code against a pinned API, but this is specialization rather than a broad first-version-aware claim.

references.title: Mokav: Execution-driven differential testing with LLMs
references.metadata_evidence: Author arXiv record confirms all four authors, JSS2025 journal reference and journal DOI. Publisher search record gives volume230/article112571; direct publisher open returned403. ArXiv title capitalization is Differential Testing; publisher uses differential testing.
references.relevance: LLM-guided differential test generation uses execution feedback to expose behavioral differences between paired programs.
references.difference_to_our_claim: Our output is a source repair judged against curated artifact obligations, not a new test-generation algorithm or generic behavioral difference detector.

references.title: ChangeGuard: Validating Code Changes via Pairwise Learning-Guided Execution
references.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (PACMSE), FSE 2025
references.metadata_evidence: Original revised paper header confirms authors, PACMSE volume2 FSE and DOI; arXiv comments confirm FSE2025 acceptance. Direct ACM landing page returned403. No page range is required for this short citation.
references.relevance: Pairwise execution can assess whether a code change alters behavior, with explicit comparison against regression tests.
references.difference_to_our_claim: Behavioral preservation checking is prior work; our limited observation contract permits specified intentional changes and cannot prove general semantic equivalence.

references.title: test(ci): detect persisted settings compatibility regressions
references.author_identity_note: Verified GitHub PR author handle; do not invent a personal name. May cite corporate author OpenHands software-agent-sdk contributors instead.
references.metadata_evidence: Original PR author/title/merge date verified. Issue3088 states motivation; merged implementation validates golden schema fixtures and payloads from a real PyPI baseline, constrains dependency resolution to the release date and preserves sentinel values. PR link is stable; current-main code URL is mutable.
references.relevance: Strong practical prior for real-release persisted-payload replay and compatibility CI, including silent-value-loss checks.
references.difference_to_our_claim: Cross-project agent repair tasks with shipped obligations and complete patch measurements may be new curation. Real-release replay and sentinel preservation themselves are not new. This source is code evidence, not peer review or evidence of our resource's adoption.
